articles.headline: Oregon QB Dante Moore won't return this season from his concussion
keyFacts: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a concussion, coach Dan Lanning announced.
Moore suffered the concussion on September 26 against USC after taking an illegal hit while sliding, which required hospital transport.
Lanning stated that Moore is expected to make a full recovery and can return to college football in 2027.
body: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who entered the season as one of the top prospects in the 2027 draft, will not play again during the 2026 season.
Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore's concussion from last month will sideline him for the balance of the schedule .

"If it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said. "This isn't a selfish decision on Dante's part, saying, 'I don't want to come back, the season doesn't look the way I want it to look.' That's not at all what this is."

Lanning said that Moore has not been cleared to return from the concussion suffered on September 26 against USC. After taking an illegal hit while sliding, Moore was taken to a local hospital by ambulance for evaluation.

"We said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to fully recover from, that hasn't changed," Lanning said. "But for him to be out there on the field for us, that's not going to happen. We'd love to have Dante out there, he's still going to be a big part of this team."
The Ducks entered the season ranked No. 2. They're now 4-3 and out of the top 25.
Under the NCAA's new five-year rule, Moore can return to college football in 2027, delaying his entry to the draft until 2028.

articles.headline: Christian Yelich sounds off on Brewers’ unreal 8-run inning vs. Rays
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 to take a 3-0 lead in the World Series.
Milwaukee scored eight runs with two outs in the fifth inning following a key hit by Brice Turang, according to Christian Yelich.
The Brewers will attempt to win their first franchise championship in Game 4 on Tuesday night.
body: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Christian Yelich sounds off on Brewers’ unreal 8-run inning vs. Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3 by a final score of 10-1. Milwaukee now holds a 3-0 World Series lead. Although it sounds like an extremely lopsided affair, the game was competitive up until the 5th inning, as Freddy Peralta and Robert Gasser were locked in a pitcher’s duel in a 2-0 game. The Brewers broke through in the 5th with an eight-run inning — with each run coming while there were two outs. Christian Yelich — who went 2-3 with an RBI in the game and played a role in the massive inning — discussed how Milwaukee found its rhythm in the 5th, via MLB Network.
“It was just good at-bat after good at-bat. Guys staying within themselves,” Yelich said. “Having an AB, competing up there, doing what we’ve done all year.”

With the score still 2-0, Brice Turang came to the plate with the bases loaded and hit a hard line drive up the middle. The ball took a tough hop to the left of Rays shortstop Taylor Walls. Walls got a glove on it, but the ball got past the shortstop and Milwaukee scored two runs on the play.

articles.headline: 8 Most Entertaining Sci-Fi Books of the 21st Century That Are Impossible to Put Down
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of eight entertaining 21st-century science fiction books that combine humor and adventure with modern social commentary.
The featured titles include comedic novels like John Scalzi's Redshirts and Andy Weir's buddy comedy Project Hail Mary.
Adaptations for some of the featured book series are currently in development for streaming platforms.
body: Science fiction writers imagine humanity's future in order to explore our present and past. The best sci-fi is a mix of cautionary tale and social commentary, but books about heady topics like artificial intelligence, alien encounters, and galaxy-spanning wars are often filled with dense explanations of theoretical technologies or complex political factions. It doesn't have to be that way. While dry and heavy sci-fi can be extremely rewarding to read, the genre also offers plenty of lighter options filled with humor and adventure. If you want some laughs in your future, check out these eight extremely fun sci-fi books that grapple with modern issues facing humanity in the 21st Century.
8 Redshirts by John Scalzi (2012)

John Scalzi is a master of comedic sci-fi, whether penning zany novels like Starter Villain or the silly short stories that got adapted to episodes of the Netflix anthology series Love, Death & Robots. Fans of Star Trek: Lower Decks should check out his Hugo Award-winning novel Redshirts, which follows a group of new ensigns on a starship where away missions have an appallingly high casualty rate. Things get far weirder when the new crew begins investigating the nature of their ship’s confrontations with aggressive aliens and looking for a way to save their lives.
7 The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet by Becky Chambers (2014)

Very much a journey over destination book, Becky Chambers’ originally self-published debut novel follows Rosemary Harper, a woman from Mars who tries to escape her past by joining the crew of a ship tasked with tunneling wormholes through space. Rosemary learns a lot from the quirky aliens she shares the ship with as they protect each other in this sweet story of found family. The cozy book is a perfect read for fans of Firefly or Farscape.
6 Artificial Condition by Martha Wells (2018)

The Murderbot Diaries is a hilarious series about Murderbot, a rogue cyborg security guard who would rather be watching soap operas than protecting dumb, helpless humans. While Murderbot’s running internal monologue is always entertaining, the second book in Martha Wells’ series is one of the best. Murderbot gets the perfect foil in an advanced ship AI dubbed Asshole Research Transport. As Murderbot tries to learn more about its past, it has to put up with a new friend who wants to share TV time. Read Artificial Condition before watching the second season of the Apple TV adaptation, which is currently in the works.
5 Space Opera by Catherynne M. Valente (2018)

The space opera genre gets literal in Catherynne M. Valente's absurdist book where humanity has to compete in the Metagalactic Grand Prix, a Eurovision-like song contest. Filled with over-the-top humor, Space Opera is basically a glam rock tribute to The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy. The washed-up band Decibel Jones and the Absolute Zeroes has to use music to prove humanity is actually sentient, and if they place last, the whole species will be destroyed.
4 Chilling Effect by Valerie Valdes (2019)

Space operas often feature oddball ensembles, but few are as weird as the crew of La Sirena Negra. The foul-mouthed captain Eva Innocente is on a mission to save her kidnapped sister, and she’s lying to her crew about the stakes as she leads them on a series of dangerous jobs so she can pay the ransom. The book pokes fun at video games and pop culture as Eva has to deal with psychic cats and the unwanted affection of an alien emperor.
3 Gideon the Ninth by Tamsyn Muir (2019)

While the first book in Tamsyn Muir’s The Locked Tomb science fantasy series is a very bloody mystery, Gideon’s snarky humor keeps the story from ever feeling too heavy. Gideon is tasked with protecting the necromancer Harrow as the heirs of the empire’s great houses complete challenges to prove they are worthy of immortality. Donning skull makeup and aviator shades, Gideon is perpetually exasperating Harrow, though the two need to work together to survive and figure out who is killing the other competitors.
2 Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir (2021)

Andy Weir’s debut novel, The Martian, is surprisingly fun for a story about a stranded astronaut trying to grow potatoes so he doesn’t starve to death. Weir’s followup, Project Hail Mary, is even more entertaining as Weir applies his signature dry wit and skill at explaining hard science to a buddy comedy adventure rather than a survival story. Science teacher and biologist Ryland Grace wakes up with amnesia on a spaceship orbiting a distant star, discovering he’s the only survivor of a mission to save Earth’s sun from being consumed. Luckily he finds an unlikely ally — an alien who is trying to save his own planet. The book got a perfect adaptation in 2026, but it’s still worth reading for some wild moments that didn’t make it into the film.
1 Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman (2024)

Matt Dinniman popularized LitRPGs with his self-published Dungeon Crawler Carl series, which got a commercial printing in 2024. Blending science fiction and fantasy, the series follows Carl, a Coast Guard veteran who winds up competing in an alien reality TV show along with his ex-girlfriend’s prized show cat. The dynamic between the unlikely party members is hilarious as they have to face bizarre challenges to level up, impress a twisted AI, and build a following among viewers from across the galaxy. Seth MacFarlane is working on an adaptation of the series for Peacock.

articles.headline: Brazil elections: Merz, world leaders congratulate Lula on his win
keyFacts: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff election with 51.7% of the vote, official results showed.
Brazilian stocks fell nearly 17% and triggered a trading halt, while Bolsonaro's party recognized Lula's victory.
Bolsonaro vowed to seek the annulment of the election result, claiming that voting hour extensions favored Lula.
body: What you need to know
- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro
- It was a tight runoff, with Lula winning 51.7% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.2%, official results showed
- In his victory speech, Lula urged more regulation of big tech platforms after allegations that Meta interfered in the race
- Bolsonaro refused to concede, but his party recognizes Lula's victory
- Trading was suspended on the stock market for half an hour on Monday morning as shares and Brazil's real currency tumbled
- Several Latin American leaders congratulated Lula on win
- Germany's Merz said he looks forward to 'deepening strategic ties' with Brazil
- US President Trump said the vote 'looked terrible,' but added, 'I like Lula'
This blog is now closed.
Keep reading for developments from the second round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25, with continued coverage into Monday, October 26.

We're sure to have more coverage of Brazilian politics, Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro in the coming days and weeks.
Stay tuned for more with DW.
Bolsonaro's party recognizes Lula's election victory
Brazil's Liberal Party has acknowledged President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory, breaking with its own candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who has refused to concede defeat.
"We recognize the presidential election results," party leader Valdemar Costa Neto said in a statement on Monday. "But we believe the issues raised need to be properly clarified."
The statement marks a clear break with Bolsonaro's position. The senator has vowed to seek the annulment of Sunday's runoff result, claiming that a two-hour extension of voting favored Lula.

The extension was ordered due to transport problems in several cities that made it difficult for voters to reach polling stations. Bolsonaro's own campaign had also requested more voting time in some regions because of heavy rainfall.
According to electoral officials, the extension did not change the outcome of the election.
Bolsonaro has yet to publicly respond to his party's statement.
Flavio Bolsonaro says he is banned from leaving Brazil after election defeat
Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro says he has been ordered to surrender his passports and is banned from leaving the country.
The right-wing senator said federal police approached him after he visited his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
"I was ordered right on the street to hand over my passports, and I'm also prohibited from leaving the country," Bolsonaro said in a video posted on social media.

He called the move "a clear attempt to intimidate me" and claimed the order came from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Neither the court nor federal police immediately confirmed the reported ruling.

Bolsonaro said the decision was based on comments by his brother Eduardo, who had suggested he should leave Brazil if he lost the election. He denied having any plans to flee the country and said he would comply with the order.
Trump says Brazil vote 'looked terrible to me' but adds, 'I like Lula'
Ask, and you shall receive — sometimes anyway! Now a senior US government representative has commented on Brazil's vote.
Leaving Washington for a midterm election campaign rally, President Donald Trump told reporters that it "looked terrible" to him.
"I didn't take sides but it looked like another rigged election frankly... it looked so corrupt, so terrible," he said.
Asked by a reporter if he wanted to "do something about the election," Trump seemed to suggest he did not, albeit repeating his criticism of the mechanics of the vote.

"Well, I'm not running Brazil. I'm running the USA. I just thought that the election was, uh — I like Lula, I get along with him very well — I just think it had a very bad look, the election. The way it was tabulated, you know? The extension given was very strange."
US yet to comment on Brazil election
As of 3:20 p.m. in Washington D.C. (1920 GMT), the upper echelons of US government were yet to respond to the election in Brazil on Sunday.

The only October 26 State Department press releases concerned Austria's national day and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's planned trip to Georgia later in the week for a G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting.

Rubio had not opined on his social media channels and US President Donald Trump's Truth Social account — which only tends to pick up on stories with a tape delay unless they involve Trump directly — had remained inactive since Sunday night.
Lula and his Workers' Party often had strained relations with US governments, especially Republican ones, but this has been particularly pronounced in Trump's case.
Recap — Why is Bolsonaro crying foul after the voting extension?

Just joining us and wondering how Brazil's runoff vote had a considerably clearer margin of victory than predicted and yet still ended in controversy and the losing candidate refusing to concede defeat?
Challenger Flavio Bolsonaro's objections were focused around the evening extension of voting past the planned closing time of 5 p.m. across the country.

The decisions by a Lula-appointed Supreme Court justice on Sunday followed a complaint over allegations of pro-Bolsonaro mayors being behind public transport irregularities that may have hampered people's plans to vote.
On election night, Bolsonaro then told journalists it was "impossible to recognize the election results, given the circumstances under which things unfolded."
For now it's unclear whether, as the dust settles, Bolsonaro will continue to resist the outcome and try to encourage protests in the way his now-jailed father Jair Bolsonaro did four years ago.
But two factors in particular seem to speak against the prospects of a potential Bolsonaro challenge.

Firstly, his fairly sizeable margin of defeat — losing by slightly more than 4 million votes rather than just a few thousand — makes it much more unlikely that a two-hour extension at polling stations could have even the theoretical potential of swaying the result.

And beyond that, his camp appealed for and successfully secured permission to keep polling stations open in some of Bolsonaro's southern strongholds, after torrential rains interfered with would-be voters' travel plans.
African leaders congratulate Lula, seek to 'advance shared interests'
Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was one of several African leaders to congratulate Lula on Monday, saying that his renewed mandate offered an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties.

"As two leading nations of the Global South, we can promote economic integration and advance our shared interests in a rapidly changing global order," Tinubu said online, saying he looked forward to expanding cooperation in a raft of areas.
Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu also extended her "sincere congratulations" to Lula.

"Tanzania values its longstanding friendship with Brazil, and looks forward to continue building on this foundation to further strengthen bilateral relations and deepen cooperation, for the mutual benefit of our two nations," Suluhu said.

Seychelles President Patrick Herminie called the runoff election result "a powerful affirmation of the trust the Brazilian people have placed in President Lula's leadership," in comments published by his office online.

He said Lula's win was "a testament to his lifelong commitment to the dignity and well-being of ordinary men and women," saying the Seychelles shared Lula's values like "social justice, equality of opportunity, the protection of workers and the most vulnerable, and a model of development that places people at its center."
Herminie expressed a desire to deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in tackling climate change, protecting the oceans and advancing the interests of the Global South.
Putin congratulates Lula, praising his 'personal contribution' to bilateral ties
Russian President Vladimir Putin offered congratulations to Lula in a telegram published by the Kremlin on Monday.
"It is difficult to overstate your personal contribution to strengthening the strategic partnership between Brazil and Russia," the telegram stated.
Putin, a leader of a fellow BRICS alliance member, is one of few world leaders to have worked with Lula across all of his presidential terms, starting in 2003.
Putin also congratulated Lula on his upcoming 81st birthday, which falls on Tuesday.
The Russian president's spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow earlier in the day that the Kremlin welcomed Lula's re-election.
WATCH: Brazil's Lula celebrates election victory as Bolsonaro rejects results
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term after defeating far-right rival Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff election.
It's a historic political comeback for Lula who trailed in the first round.
DW reports from Rio de Janeiro.
Sao Paulo stock exchange halts trading over sharp drop after Lula win

Trading on the Sao Paulo stock exchange, the largest in Latin America, was suspended for 30 minutes on Monday after plummeting nearly 17% in the wake of the re-election of left-wing Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who defeated conservative Flavio Bolsonaro.
The sharp drop in the benchmark Ibovespa index triggered a 30-minute "circuit breaker" mechanism provided for "periods of sharp market decline," according to a stock exchange statement.
Meanwhile, the US dollar surged 12% against Brazil's currency, one of the real's biggest daily moves on record.
Prices of raw sugar, one of Brazil's most important exports, slid nearly 5% on the collapsing exchange rate.
Prediction markets had indicated a Bolsonaro win but the right-wing senator's refusal to concede defeat and his pledge to challenge the election result have added to investor uncertainty.

"Important for local financial markets will be how quickly Bolsonaro accepts the result, or at least allows the constitution to run its course," Chris Turner, a strategist at ING in London, told the Reuters news agency as attention turned to Lula's choice of finance minister — a clue as to his fiscal approach.

"The key signal for markets will be the next Lula administration's commitment to fiscal discipline, starting with the appointment of a new finance minister in coming weeks," RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Graham Stock told Reuters.
Germany's Merz wants to deepen 'the strategic partnership' with Brazil
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has joined the chorus of world leaders congratulating Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election.
"I look forward to further deepening the strategic partnership between Germany and Brazil together," Merz said in a message posted on X.
Germany and Brazil held government consultations in Hannover in April of this year, at which Merz and Lula agreed to cooperate more closely on defense and raw materials, among other things.
Brazilian markets poised for sharp drop Monday after Lula win
Brazilian markets are bracing for heavy selling on Monday, with futures of Brazil's benchmark stock index Bovespa falling nearly 15% in early Monday trading
On global markets, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, which tracks a basket of major Brazilian stocks, plunged as much as 26% in premarket trading as investors unwind bets on a right-wing victory.

Brazilian Real November futures also fell 10% in Asian trading, while US-listed shares of Brazilian stocks dropped as well, with energy giant Petrobras plunging more than 20% and banking group Itau Unibanco cratering almost 30%.

Investors had seen election loser Flavio Bolsonaro as the candidate most likely to boost markets with fiscal austerity and deregulation, while Lula has pursued policies of redistribution and state-led development, including costly welfare programs.
Russia says it welcomes Lula's re-election
The Kremlin said on Monday it welcomed Lula's victory and praised what it said were his efforts to cultivate Brazil-Russia ties.

"We welcome Mr. Lula's victory. He does a lot, not only for the development of bilateral relations but also for advancing processes within the framework of BRICS," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
He said Russia hoped for more of the same.
Lula himself has possibly put Brazil in the Kremlin's good books by not joining Western sanctions on Russia over Moscow's invasion of Ukraine and calling for a negotiated peace.
However, he has called on all nations to adhere to the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity enshrined in the UN Charter, thus implicitly condemning Russia's aggression.

Brazil and Russia are both members of BRICS, an international cooperation group founded in 2009 along with India and China, with South Africa joining a year later, and taking all those countries' first initials to make up its name.
It has since then been expanded to include 10 member nations in all, with a number of "partner countries" also invited in 2024.

France, China, Spain congratulate Lula on victory
Messages of congratulations continue to rain in from around the world following Lula's unexpected win.

China's response was measured, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying that "China has noted that Brazil's Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations."
Guo added that Beijing was "willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future."
French President Emmanuel Macron, after expressing his congratulations, said Brazil and France should work to "strengthen our strategic partnership."
"France and Brazil have much to build together," Macron said X, adding that the two countries should nurture their friendship "in the service of a fairer world."
Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, was more effusive, casting Lula's victory as evidence that the world is experiencing a backlash to its seeming rightwards political trajectory at present.
"A great victory for Lula! What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The global progressive comeback has just begun," Sanchez, who has called snap elections in November, posted on X.

articles.headline: Eagles’ nightmare season deepens as Cowboys hand Philadelphia fifth straight loss
keyFacts: Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns as the Dallas Cowboys defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night.
The loss handed the Eagles their fifth consecutive defeat, dropping their record to 2-5 in a season impacted by injuries.
Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season because of blood clots in his lungs.
body: Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns, two to CeeDee Lamb, and the Dallas Cowboys beat Philadelphia 38-21 on Monday night to hand the Eagles their fifth straight loss.
Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown, and the Cowboys (3-4) remained in contention for the NFC East title. The New York Giants lead the division at 4-2-1.
The Eagles (2-5) are spiraling into a disaster of a season with their longest skid since 2016.

Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season because of blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee provided little encouragement that he can turn the season around, completing 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception.
Prescott finished long drives with scores that McKee was unable to match.

With Dallas trailing 21-20 late in the third quarter, Lamb hauled in his second touchdown on a beautiful 16-yard floater from Prescott in the corner of the end zone. Prescott ran in the two-point conversion for a 28-21 lead.

Brandon Aubrey kicked field goals of 55, 27 and 24 yards. The final kick extended Dallas’ lead to 31-21. Williams capped the scoring and the first 150-yard rushing game by a Dallas player since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018 with a two-yard touchdown. The Cowboys finished with 204 yards rushing.
McKee had a pass intercepted by linebacker DeMarvion Overshown late in the fourth quarter.

McKee orchestrated the Eagles’ first touchdown drive in the third quarter this season when they ran almost 10 minutes off the clock and he hit rookie Makai Lemon for a four-yard touchdown and a 21-20 lead.
The Eagles didn’t score again and are running out of time to salvage their season.

The Cowboys got a field goal on the opening drive, and the Eagles came right back and made it 7-3 on Saquon Barkley’s eight-yard touchdown run. Barkley returned after missing the last two-plus games with a hamstring injury and had 37 yards rushing on the drive.

Barkley entered with 36 yards rushing all season. He still seemed bothered by the hamstring and had to visit the sideline medical tent. Barkley also missed long stretches getting treatment for his back on the sideline and finished with 62 yards on seven carries.

Prescott threw touchdown passes of nine yards to Lamb and 21 yards to George Pickens that helped the Cowboys stretch their lead to 20-14 at half-time. Pickens’ catch was particularly impressive, as he escaped tight coverage by safety Andrew Mukuba in the back of the end zone and dragged his left foot sideways for the score.
At half-time, Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie was inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame.

Lurie bought the Eagles on 6 May 1994, and since the turn of the century they have been one of the top franchises in football. The Eagles are one of three teams to play in four Super Bowls since 2004 and have won the only two titles in franchise history under Lurie’s ownership.

Lurie was flanked by Eagles Hall of Famers including Brian Dawkins and Donovan McNabb and gave a brief speech. However, unlike other Hall of Fame inductees, Lurie did not hold a pre-game news conference. Coach Nick Sirianni remained the only team representative addressing Hurts’ condition since he was injured.

articles.headline: DHS suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals amid birth tourism, security concerns
keyFacts: The Department of Homeland Security is suspending a visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals visiting the Northern Mariana Islands.
DHS cited concerns that the program facilitates birth tourism, espionage, and illegal onward travel to nearby Guam.
The suspension takes effect on October 30 while DHS evaluates the policy with other departments, the agency said.
body: DHS suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals amid birth tourism, security concerns
By
Stepheny Price, Bill Melugin, Fox News
Published Oct. 27, 2026, 12:23 a.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The Trump administration is suspending a visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals visiting a US island territory after Republican lawmakers warned it could facilitate birth tourism and pose national security risks.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s decision targets a Biden-era program that allowed prescreened Chinese nationals to visit the Northern Mariana Islands for up to 14 days without a visa.

In a notice announcing the decision, the Department of Homeland Security cited concerns that the program could facilitate birth tourism, espionage and illegal onward travel to nearby Guam, a key hub for the US military.

The decision comes after senators Mike Lee, R-Utah, Rick Scott, R-Fla., John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Bill Cassidy, R-La., urged Mullin in April to end the program, warning that it encouraged birth tourism and posed national security risks.
Lee celebrated the decision in a post on X.
“America is not a nursery for the CCP to steal citizenship,” Lee wrote, referring to the Chinese Communist Party. “Thank you, President Trump!”
Rep. Chip Roy’s press office also welcomed the move, saying the Texas Republican and Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wis., had raised concerns about the program in March.
“Rep. Roy is pleased to hear the Trump Admin closed this dangerous loophole,” his office wrote on X.

Birth tourism is when someone travels to the United States primarily to give birth so their child can become an American citizen. Some travelers have hidden the purpose of their trip when applying for a visa.
The program at issue was created in 2024 and took effect the following year. More than 3,000 Chinese nationals used it to enter the Northern Mariana Islands in fiscal year 2025, according to DHS.
Those travelers were screened by Customs and Border Protection, but did not have to obtain a visa through a US consulate, the department said.
The suspension is set to take effect at 2 p.m. EDT on Oct. 30 and will apply to both new applicants and travelers who have already been approved.
Those already in the territory under the program may finish their authorized stays but will need a visa for future visits unless another lawful exception applies.
DHS said the suspension will remain in place while the department evaluates the program with the secretaries of state and the interior.
The department warned that the program could make it easier for Chinese nationals to travel to the territory to give birth.
“While birth tourism has long been an issue in the CNMI, the availability of visa-exempt travel and reduced vetting under EVS-TAP may lower barriers to this practice,” the notice says.

DHS also said birth tourism can strain the islands’ medical system. The notice did not provide a number of births linked to travelers who entered through the program, formally known as the Economic Vitality & Security Travel Authorization Program.

The department warned that visa-free travel could be exploited for intelligence gathering near USAlthough the program did not permit visitors to travel to Guam or the US.mainland, DHS cited previous cases involving Chinese nationals smuggled by boat from the Northern Mariana Islands to Guam.
Those cases involved earlier travel policies or other streamlined arrangements, but DHS said they showed a vulnerability that the newer program had not eliminated.

The suspension comes as the Trump administration pursues a broader crackdown on birth tourism. A State Department task force launched Aug. 12 had revoked more than 750 visas tied to suspected birth tourism activity as of late August, the department previously told Fox News Digital.

State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott told Fox News Digital that officials were working with international partners and law enforcement to identify travel patterns that could point to birth tourism networks.
Pigott said some networks help visitors conceal the purpose of their trips and then coach them on how to avoid paying medical bills.

The Northern Mariana Islands program is separate from the visitor visa process targeted by those revocations. military facilities. The Northern Mariana Islands are home to Tinian Air Base, while Guam hosts several military installations.

articles.headline: Jackson Chourio just showing off now as the face of the Brewers as Crew creeps closer to World Series title
keyFacts: The Brewers defeated the Rays 10-1 in Game 3 to take a 3-0 lead in the World Series.
Twenty-two-year-old Jackson Chourio recorded four hits for the Brewers, becoming the youngest player with a four-hit World Series game since 1946.
The Brewers can secure a sweep and win the World Series with a victory in Game 4.
body: ST. PETERSBURG -- Game 3 of the World Series was a total bloodbath. The Brewers now have a 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series after a 10-1 drubbing of whatever is left of the Rays. Pick your phrase: men vs. boys, varsity vs. JV. This has been less a series than an inevitability.

The Brewers are now 7-0 in the NLCS and World Series. The only team previously to sweep both of the last two rounds was the 1976 Reds, but that Big Red Machine only had a five-game NLCS. The Brewers can make it 8-0 for the first time in MLB history with a win in Game 4.

First things first, though. Let's discuss this Game 3 monstrosity from the Crew. They recorded 10 runs on 16 hits, compared to 1 and 3 from the Rays -- and it was worse than it looked because the Rays got a run on two hits in the ninth when it was already basically over. It was domination from start to finish, while the Rays were bumbling and ineffectual. Front and center for the winners? Jackson Chourio, of course.

Heading into the series, I noted that Chourio and Rays third baseman Junior Caminero were . Chourio has been up to the task and then some. He led off the game with a line drive single, then came through with singles in each of his next two at-bats, too. In his fourth at-bat, he doubled during the game-changing, eight-run fifth inning.

"Yeah, I think that you could say this is one of my better games," Chourio said after the game. "Really, I was just taking every at-bat like it could be my last and trying to find any way I could to get on base. Because I know, as long as I get on base, there's guys behind me who could score."

That fifth-inning double was the weakest of his four hits at 99 mph (95+ are considered "hard hit" balls). Chourio put up four hits, two runs and an RBI through five innings. The Rays as a team recorded zero runs on one hit through eight.

Remember, Chourio is still only 22 years old. In Game 3, he became the youngest player with a four-hit World Series game since Joe Garagiola in 1946. It was the first time in 80 years! That's how talented this wunderkind is.

"Nobody's surprised that Jack Jack's doing this. Nobody's surprised. He's turning into -- 20, 21, 22, he's turning into a fine player. He's understanding what it takes, the discipline that it takes. He's coming into his own. Nobody's shocked. He's just really, really good," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Game 3.

"He's also played incredible defense, and he stole a base tonight. He's a total player. Like we talked about, you ask about Kobe Bryant and him. Kobe strived to get better and better and better every year because he was so disciplined. He was such a worker. He had such an attitude. Jackson's on that same track."

The Brewers churn out talent from all over the spectrum. They get the absolute most out of retreads like Jake Bauers, as well as organizational guys like Game 3 starter Robert Gasser. And then there are superstar prospects like Chourio.

He won't finish that high in MVP voting this season, but it might be the last time for a long time. Injury held him to 127 games this season and he still posted 4.9 WAR. He's gone 20-20 (home runs and steals) in three seasons already. We've seen all five tools in the playoffs.

The hit tool? Yeah, he's 8 for 14 in the World Series, good for a cool .571 average. Power? He's hit two home runs in the postseason so far. Speed? He stole a base in Game 3, giving him three World Series steals so far. The glove and arm were on display in Game 2, when he threw out an all-important Rays baserunner at home.

When you watch Chourio play, he makes you feel like there's nothing he can't do on a baseball field. It's true, and he's only starting to scratch the proverbial surface. He wouldn't be a bad prediction for National League MVP next season. But first, he's strutting his stuff on the biggest stage.

Anyone who has watched him play regularly isn't surprised one bit by the performance in this World Series. He's long had the talent and confidence and swagger of a superstar. And just as importantly, he's signed with the Brewers on a team-friendly deal through the 2031 season with two more club options running through 2033. He's poised to be the face of the organization for a long time.

The Brewers are better in every facet, and the Rays blew their only opening in three games so far when they put up four runs in the first inning of Game 2, then failed to score again in a 5-4 loss. Hell, they haven't scored since. And they got the doors blown off them in Game 3 by the superior team. In the case of men vs. boys here, one of the youngest players in the series is the biggest, baddest man of all.

articles.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon may be overkill for most tasks
keyFacts: Google released its Gemini 4 Argon AI model, which offers advanced reasoning and problem-solving capabilities suitable for complex tasks like quantum computing research.
TechRadar reported that the model's immense power may be unnecessary for average users who only need help with basic tasks like writing emails or recipes.
Google and other AI developers face the challenge of helping users easily recognize which specific assignments actually justify using their most powerful models.
body: Google's latest AI model can untangle millions of lines of code and accelerate quantum computing research, which is great if you happen to spend your afternoons debugging enormous software projects or advancing theoretical physics. For the average Gemini user, the sheer power of the new Gemini 4 Argon model begs the question: why do you need it?

Google has made Gemini 4 Argon readily available in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers. Simply pick it from the list of models available at the top of the conversation. Google brags about the model's advanced reasoning, multi-step problem-solving, and other improvements provided by the sophisticated AI, but it's a little much for helping write an email.

Whether Argon can outperform its predecessors on complicated benchmarks is less interesting than figuring out what to do with all this additional AI power. As AI models become increasingly specialized, we may be approaching a point where the technology is advancing faster than people's ability to understand why they need it.
Give the big model a big problem

Gemini 4 Argon certainly has potential uses, for instance, in analyzing complicated information scattered across several files. Imagine comparing three health insurance policies with different deductibles, premiums, coverage exclusions, and out-of-pocket limits. A regular Gemini model can already summarize the policies, but Argon's advanced reasoning could become valuable when calculating how different combinations of medical expenses would affect the total annual cost. It would be great at navigating all kinds of potential healthcare scenarios, tracking multiple interacting variables, identifying relevant exceptions, and calculating their consequences.

The same principle applies to any other complicated project, like renovating a house and asking the model to evaluate contractor estimates, material costs, and architectural plans for inconsistencies and potential price overruns. Argon 4 might help when determining how a delayed electrical inspection affects several subsequent jobs and the overall budget.

It could also be useful in learning complicated academic subjects that incorporate a lot of interconnected concepts, such as advanced math. All of that is still only potentially better than simply using the less powerful models. It might be as complicated to work out when Argon 4 is necessary as the very projects for which the model is best suited.
Overthinking AI

It sometimes feels ridiculous how Google is building models capable of tackling extraordinary scientific and engineering challenges, then placing them in the same interface people use to request pancake recipes. The technology is becoming increasingly sophisticated, yet the reasons to choose one model over another remain vague.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

This is hardly unique to Google. OpenAI and Anthropic have their own incredibly powerful models that seem ill-suited to the average user. The most powerful model isn't always going to be the most useful. Asking Gemini to rewrite an email or suggest dinner ideas probably doesn't require Argon's additional reasoning capabilities. A faster model might deliver an equally useful answer faster. Even the more complicated examples aren't necessarily beyond ordinary Gemini models. Argon's advantage would need to come from handling unusually complicated combinations of constraints.
The challenge for Google is that users can't easily recognize which assignments justify a more powerful model. In that case, the model picker becomes an annoyance and not a feature.

Right now, most Gemini users should stick to the less intense models and reserve Gemini 4 Argon for assignments where they would struggle. Argon 4 is apparently a remarkable technical achievement with huge possible benefits in some research, but I don't need something capable of solving quantum computing problems on an everyday basis. AI developers have become very good at building models capable of extraordinary work, but the most impressive feat would be explaining when ordinary people actually need them.

Eric Hal Schwartz is a freelance writer for TechRadar with more than 15 years of experience covering the intersection of the world and technology. For the last five years, he served as head writer for Voicebot.ai and was on the leading edge of reporting on generative AI and large language models. He's since become an expert on the products of generative AI models, such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Google Gemini, and every other synthetic media tool. His experience runs the gamut of media, including print, digital, broadcast, and live events. Now, he's continuing to tell the stories people want and need to hear about the rapidly evolving AI space and its impact on their lives. Eric is based in New York City.

articles.headline: This Book Release Is Basically GTA 6 Launch For Thirsty Women, And Larian Knows It
keyFacts: Developer Larian Studios shared an Instagram post referencing the A Court of Thorns and Roses book series ahead of its sixth book release.
The sixth book in the popular fantasy series, titled A Court of Splintered Harmony, releases later tonight.
Larian's social media post featured characters in Baldur's Gate 3's creator making inside jokes and poking fun at moments from the book series.
body: You might have noticed that Baldur's Gate 3 has an extraordinarily large female audience, and for years, I've had my own theory as to why this is. Much like Dragon Age ( rest in peace, my sweet angel ), Baldur's Gate 3 features high stakes, fantasy-filled adventure, swords and sorcery, and charming characters that you can smooch. Essentially, it's a Romantasy--a term given to the plethora of women-oriented novels that feature all of the above.

Regardless of if you love or hate the term, Romantasy has exploded in popularity over the past decade, and part of that is thanks to writer Sarah J. Maas and her A Court of Thorns and Roses series. For over five years, that series has been on hold while Maas worked on other novels, but now, the sixth book in the series, A Court of Splintered Harmony, is finally here--or at least it will be later tonight. Anyways, it's basically GTA 6 release day for thirsty women, and Larian's latest post proves that team is well aware of it.

Earlier today, Larian took to Instagram to share a post referencing the series ahead of A Court of Splintered Harmony's release. In it, the studio shows off a few of the saga's most notable characters in Baldur's Gate 3's character creator while ACOTAR-related audio plays over top.

But while Larian celebrating ACOTAR was already enough to made me giddy, the best thing about this post is that it proves that someone at Larian knows ball . Each clip perfectly pokes fun at a character's most iconic (or notorious) moment, or references an inside joke from the ACOTAR community. This includes Feyre's watery bowels, the invisible fleck of dust Rhysand is constantly picking at, and the fact that Feyre's garden-loving sister Elain probably could have helped her family and grown a few crops while they were, you know, starving to death in a small cottage. And the Withers-Suriel comparison? Masterful.

Suffice to say that as both an avid reader and gamer, Larian's post delighted me. And as someone who has been yelling about how many of the best games around are secretly Romantasy games (The Witcher 3, The Blood of Dawnwalker, just about every Final Fantasy...), you have no idea how validated I feel right now.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks further changes to DC golf course
keyFacts: A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction barring the federal government from removing additional trees at East Potomac Golf Links.
The DC Preservation League and two golfers sued, claiming officials violated environmental laws by cutting trees without an environmental review.
The injunction remains until final judgment, delaying work planned for November 15, while the Department of Justice may appeal.
body: A Biden-appointed federal judge issued a preliminary injunction on Monday, prohibiting the Trump administration from removing more trees at East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes determined the administration likely violated federal environmental law, as argued by the plaintiffs, by cutting down trees at the golf course without conducting an environmental review on the renovation plan.

“Plaintiffs will be imminently and irreparably harmed if the Court does not act,” Reyes wrote . “And there is no equitable reason to permit the Government to continue removing trees pending litigation given its conceded lack of any urgency to do so.”

The National Park Service , which falls under the Interior Department , planned to implement President Donald Trump’s vision of turning the public course into an 18-hole championship venue. Before the judge intervened, the agency removed hundreds of trees to pave the way for construction next month. Officials intended to cut more trees until Reyes halted the project to consider the legal challenge brought by the DC Preservation League and two longtime golfers.

In addition to barring further tree removal, the order requires the federal government to provide a written notice 10 days in advance of “any irreparable modification to any forms or features of East Potomac Park.”
The indefinite block means Trump likely won’t see the planned restoration work on the golf course start by Nov. 15.

The preliminary injunction arrived hours before the judge’s temporary restraining order was set to expire, and it will remain in effect until a final judgment is given. The Department of Justice may appeal the latest order.

Federal attorneys have sparred with Reyes during contentious court hearings, where the judge rebuked government lawyers for failing to notify the court before the initial wave of tree removal occurred earlier this month. Meanwhile, the DOJ has accused Reyes of exemplifying judicial bias against the administration.

In her memorandum opinion, Reyes expressed her frustrations with the government’s representations about the legal dispute, saying the DOJ has either rarely or never “urged a federal court not to believe the sitting President.” There were apparent conflicting accounts between the DOJ and Trump that Reyes questioned. She also wondered whether the DOJ intentionally failed to notify the court before plaintiffs filed their emergency request.

“The Government appears to have set the timing of the tree removal and late notice to impede Plaintiffs’ ability to seek Court intervention,” the Biden appointee said. “And its recent actions call into question other representations it has made to the Court over these many months.”
Reyes ended the preliminary injunction with an amusing statement, referencing a past comment she made about not comparing herself to Dr. Seuss’s Lorax character.
“The Court earlier stated, ‘I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees,'” she wrote. “The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law.”
JUDGE WALKS BACK ‘UNTENABLE’ ORDER AGAINST TRUMP DOJ AFTER TENSE DC GOLF COURSE HEARING
Democracy Forward, which is one of the legal organizations representing the plaintiffs, praised the judge’s ruling.

“We are grateful the court intervened to prevent this lawless administration from making further irreversible changes to this precious public space,” the group said in a statement . “East Potomac Park is an important part of our history and our laws prevent this administration from depriving the public of this space without a fair and public process. We are eager to continue to argue this case in court.”

articles.headline: Trump doubles down on Obama criticism as his voice starts to give out amid campaign rally blitz
keyFacts: President Trump criticized former President Barack Obama during a campaign rally in Mississippi while experiencing voice strain.
Obama recently mocked Trump over White House renovations and construction during a campaign stop in Ohio.
Trump defended his White House renovations and urged supporters to vote in the upcoming midterm elections.
body: President Trump doubled down on his criticism of Barack Obama even as he struggled to keep his voice amid a nearly nonstop midterm campaign rally blitz to keep his Republicans in control of Congress.

“I should save my voice because Barack Hussein Obama, have you heard of him?” he told a crowd in Mississippi on Monday night, pointing to the former president’s Saturday claims that Trump was too concerned with White House renovations.
“I didn’t take any time,” Trump said. “I literally do it when I walk home from the Oval.”
He also blasted Obama for bringing the Cheesecake Factory into the argument, calling it “a very successful company.”
“He doesn’t like successful companies,” Trump said.
Obama, while campaigning for Democrats in Ohio Saturday, told supporters Trump “should be on HGTV” due to his focus on construction.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the 44th president added.

Trump offered a prolonged defense of his White House renovations — which have included tearing down the East Wing to build a ballroom, repairing and repainting the North Portico columns of the residence, paving over the Rose Garden and blinging out the Oval Office in gold wall fixtures — as necessary to maintain the historic property.
“Nobody loves it like I do,” he said of the White House. “Nobody loves it, and now the White House is in beautiful shape.”
“We have to have a beautiful, beautiful, well-kept White House, a symbol of our country,” he added.

His message was clear even if his voice was not. Trump has struggled to make himself heard the past few days and kept his rally in Mississippi on the shorter side — a little less than 90 minutes. His speeches usually go almost two hours.
The president acknowledged his scratchy sound as he implored the MAGA faithful to come out and vote in next week’s election.
“God didn’t make your vocal cords to do a rally every day, but when you love the people, it’s fine — and we love you, we really do,” the president said.
Trump is moving through a whirlwind travel schedule, taking him to 30-plus campaign stops ahead of Election Day.
“We’ve been doing the rounds. We’ve been doing the rounds,” he said.

The president was in Georgia on Saturday and Michigan on Sunday. He has two campaign stops in Texas on Tuesday, will visit Ohio on Wednesday, rally in South Carolina on Thursday, and be in Florida on Friday.
He vowed to help Republican candidates for the next eight days.
Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.) is doing “great,” Trump said at Monday’s rally.
He argued he was in the deep-red state, which he won by almost 23 points in the 2024 election, to “make sure.”
The last time Democrats won a Senate seat in Mississippi was 1982.
“I’m here because Cindy’s doing great, but I just got to make sure I can’t take a chance,” he said.

Democrats face an uphill battle to win control of the Senate, needing victories in several red states to take the majority. But party strategists believe traditional Republican strongholds like Texas, Iowa, Ohio, Kansas and Alaska are in play.
The problem, Trump explained, is “sometimes when you think somebody’s doing so well, nobody votes. They all stay home.”
“We did a little ceasefire, which I never liked very much,” he said, calling it “sort of a waste of time. But, you know, you like to listen to professionals.”
His administration reached a cease-fire with Iran in June, but that deal quickly collapsed.
The president’s biggest applause of the night came when he made a promise close to voters’ hearts.
Musing about how he’d like to rename a river and an ocean as he renamed a gulf and a lake, the president reassured the crowd that one river is off-limits.
“I promise I will never change the name of the Mississippi,” he said as the crowd gave a thunderous roar of approval.

articles.headline: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
keyFacts: OpenAI released an always-on AI personal assistant named dots at its developer day in late September.
Alexander Embiricos said dots is available to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher for $100 a month.
OpenAI stated that dots shares the same privacy controls as ChatGPT and utilizes a proactive research feature.
body: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse.

OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots, its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines.

“There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.”

The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done.

Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding. He recalled celebrating when his wife started leaving her computer on all night so that her agents could keep working.

“On the product team, what I think about is, how do we make this intuitive and useful to people?” he told Disrupt attendees. “A lot of that isn’t building some new piece of tech into the product; it’s how you frame it to the user and how it feels.”
The path from chat bot to coding tool to personal assistant

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers. Even the name—a play on the negative space inside of OpenAI’s logo—is intended “to feel like just something that could eventually be ubiquitous.” (Asked when he learned that rival AI entrepreneur Elon Musk owns the dot.com URL, Embiricos said, “I found out very late.”)

The idea of a persistent agent is that it doesn’t need prompting. For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.

In our testing, the assistant’s ability to think ahead is apparent and often useful, but it isn’t quite there yet. It will flag calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines, but not necessarily in the most timely fashion.

“The first time it told me about one of those [conflicts]—this is like early in development—it told me three minutes before the thing,” Embiricos says of his dot. “It’s like, ‘Hey, this thing is coming up. You might want to do something about it.’ I only have three minutes!”

Embiricos expects the timing to improve over time, but the proactive approach is key to the product. “I was hearing about an engineer at a drone delivery startup, and they were saying, ‘We had this outage, and by the time I noticed that the outage was going on, my dot had already noticed the outage was happening, had already analyzed the outage, and had come to me with useful information for how we could resolve the outage.’”
Giving dot the keys

As with most AI agent use cases, there’s a tension between the personal information an AI model needs to be useful and exactly how much personal data you are exposing to a software company. Muse has been criticized for the profiles it builds of your family and friends, which the software uses to know, say, what kind of restaurant you might want to go to with a specific pal, but could also add incredible value to Meta’s advertising business. Does dots collect similar data?

“Yes, we have a thing that we built into dots, which we call proactive research,” Embiricos said. “On a cadence, it will think about what it knows about you, what is the conversation that it’s had, and then what have you given it access to that it can think about, and then it will go and research, ‘What could I do to be more helpful to you?’ And then, basically, it will propose that.”

It’s difficult to separate the data needs of the agent from that of its parent corporation. Hark, a start-up developing its own AI personal assistant, is explicit in pointing out it that it doesn’t collect data to fuel an advertising business the way that OpenAI and Meta do.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how. Still, those controls aren’t granular and the app can be pushy. For example, it refuses to accept read-only access to cloud drives.
“What I think we need to do is basically build out super, super, super granular controls,” Embiricos said, but he pointed to the model’s intelligence and discretion as the other side of this coin.

“This is actually something we kind of got some flack about when we launched,” Embiricos said. “We had really conservative defaults over what the agent would do, and it would ask for permission a lot. I remember knowing that we were going to see that feedback, but thinking, ‘This is okay, we can tune that over time.’”
Can personal AI agents scale?

The other big question about AI agents is whether they can scale. They’re fun when only a few people have them, and stories of agents snagging hard-to-get reservations abound. But businesses don’t necessarily like dealing with agents and might not be equipped to. People certainly don’t like dealing with them (note: stop having your AI agents pitch me), and Embiricos is among those people. He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”
If the AI industry is right that agents are our future, can we get there without overwhelming the infrastructure that our world currently runs on, from businesses and websites to payment networks?

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem. I probably can’t say too much here, but we’re deep in lots of conversations with payment processors.”

Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers. Giving an assistant access to my email inbox already feels like a big ask, but my bank account is off limits. For now.

articles.headline: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in Mississippi amid outcry over racist, Islamophobic attacks – as it happened
keyFacts: Donald Trump campaigned in Corinth, Mississippi, to support Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith ahead of the midterm elections.
The Justice Department charged former FBI Director James Comey with two counts of leaking information related to national defense.
Federal prosecutors will eventually have to have the criminal charges against Comey approved by a grand jury.
body: 'Nobody's ever campaigned like I have for midterms', Trump says in Mississippi

Donald Trump has taken the stage in Corinth, Mississippi at a rally in support of Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, and began by suggesting that he is determined to reverse the historical pattern that midterm elections almost always go against the party of the president elected two years earlier.
In a hoarse voice, Trump claimed that his rallies have “totally changed the dialogue” around the campaign.

Patrick Fitzgerald, Comey’s attorney, said the charges were related to a 5 October 2016 New York Times article that had already been investigated by prosecutors. The case was filed through a criminal maneuver known as an “information” – meaning it was not approved by a grand jury. While prosecutors will eventually have to have the charges approved by a grand jury, filing the charges through an information appears to have been an effort to quickly get the criminal charges in against Comey before the 10-year statute of limitations expires.

Before boarding Air Force One to fly to Mississippi for a campaign rally on Monday, Donald Trump was asked to respond to his predecessor, Barack Obama, joking over the weekend that his renovation of the White House, with “gold everywhere”, has “the White House looking like Saddam Hussein open a Cheesecake Factory.”

While rightwing media outlets have tried to cast Obama’s joke as a jibe at patrons of the restaurant chain – despite a report that his own family frequented the chain during his presidency – Cara Castronuova, a former reality TV fitness trainer now covering the White House for LindellTV, seemed to get confused about the talking point when she asked Trump for comment.
“Do you have a response to Obama,” she asked, “who made fun of the Cheesecake Factory, comparing it to the White House?”
“I’ve taken care of the White House. I fixed it with the finest artisans in the world. We’ve reskinned it. It was in horrible shape,” Trump said, in part.

“So it’s very easy for me to do,” Trump continued. “I do it very very simply because it’s my nature. You know, I’m a very clean person, and the White House was in terrible shape.”

“We have to explain that to Obama because he doesn’t understand it, because he’s not a smart guy,” Trump went on. “We have to explain to Obama that the White House is a symbol of America, and it has to be maintained properly.

The president then turned to the camera to address Obama directly through the lens. “The White House - to president Obama – is a symbol of America. It has to be clean. The columns can’t be broken. Mainers are feeling the pinch acutely, particularly as the state braces for winter, where temperatures will soon drop to below freezing.

“Why is all this happening? Because people wanted more money. Billionaires had to have more money. I mean, it just doesn’t make any sense,” Jackson said. “It could end Tuesday … when we take the Senate.”

The US Senate race in Maine is neck-and-neck, with most polls showing Jackson and Collins virtually tied. In each recent election, however, Collins has defied political gravity, and defied the odds while branding herself as an independent comfortable breaking with the rest of her party (and Trump by extension). Trump makes baseless claim Lula's victory in Brazil 'looked like another rigged election'

Speaking to reporters as he left for a campaign rally in Mississippi on Monday, Donald Trump said that the comeback victory of Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, over his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, “looked like another rigged election, frankly.”

None of the reporters in the limited press pool, after reporters from CNN and Politico were again blocked from taking part, pointed out to Trump that Brazil’s supreme court only extended voting hours across the nation by two hours after requests from both candidates.

The correspondent who was questioning Trump was Cara Castronuova a former reality TV fitness trainer now covering the White House for LindellTV, the streaming platform created by Mike Lindell, the election conspiracy theorist pillow salesman.

As our colleagues in Brazil reported earlier, the president of Brazil’s electoral court, justice Kassio Nunes Marques, who was appointed by the Bolsonaro’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, said that extending voting hours had caused “no change” to the election result.

Asked if he intended to intervene in any way, Trump said: “Well, I’m not running Brazil. I’m running the USA. And I just thought that the election was – I like Lula. I get along with him very well. body: - Published
Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets that have developed problems with their screens just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.
Photos posted on social media show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant's first ever foldable device, which has a starting price of Â£1,999 ($2,668) in the UK.
Apple said it is aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.
The Duo's launch, which attracted crowds at Apple stores around the world last week, comes as the brand tries to reinvigorate its range of devices and challenge the foldable phones made by rivals.
Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.

An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help.
The extent of the issue remains unclear. Apple did not say how many devices were affected, while some images showing faulty devices may have been created using artificial intelligence.

The Duo's 7.6-inch (19.3cm) inner display is held together by a central hinge - a complex piece of engineering that has resulted in similar flaws in folding devices made by some of Apple's competitors.
Samsung's first foldable phone, the Galaxy Fold, suffered an early setback in 2019 when reviewers reported broken screens on the devices.
Android users already have a broad selection of foldable phones to choose from, technology that Apple spent years developing before the Duo's release.
It is Apple's most expensive iPhone ever, costing up to Â£3,199 for the most well-equipped models.
The Duo marks Apple's first major iPhone redesign in almost two decades and was unveiled by new chief executive John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September.
When closed, the Duo looks like a wider version of an iPhone, then opens up to a device resembling a small tablet computer.
"Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together", Ternus told an audience at Apple's California headquarters last month.
The Duo, he said, would "redefine the experience of using a foldable phone".

articles.headline: Japanese virtual desktop cloud hacked so hard it asks to be banned
keyFacts: Japanese ISP GMO Internet warned that its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service was compromised, exposing customer trading accounts and passwords.
The attacker demanded $50 million, but GMO refused to pay and instead asked trading services to block trade requests from the cloud platform.
GMO CEO Masatoshi Kumagai stated that investigations continue, up to 26,739 servers may be affected, and the company proposed government cybersecurity action.
body: Japanese ISP GMO Internet has warned customers the cloudy desktop service it offers as an ideal foreign exchange trading environment was compromised by an attacker, and that it had been slow to improve the service's security.

GMO runs a service called Onamae.com Desktop Cloud and last week admitted “a third party had installed malicious programs in the server environments of some customers.” That’s never welcome news but is an especially poor outcome because the servers host cloudy Windows desktops that GMO recommends customers use to host foreign exchange trading applications.

In later updates the company revealed that some customers reported “unauthorized operations were performed on their trading accounts” and advised that third parties had probably seen users’ passwords for trading services.
The next day, the company advised users to immediately change passwords for their trading accounts, and to do so using a device that they don’t use for trading.

The company has since admitted that its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service’s “systems had security vulnerabilities, that its environment was accessed without authorization, and that customer information was taken outside the Company.”
“Some customers have also reported transactions in their trading accounts that they do not recognize.”

Those transactions have GMO sufficiently worried that it contacted major trading services, asked them to forcibly terminate all active sessions, monitor for unauthorized transactions, and to block trade requests coming from the Onamae.com Desktop Cloud.
Not paying, or complaining

GMO said it has “received a demand for money from a person believed to be the attacker. We have also been told that, if we refuse, the attacker will take actions such as publishing information about the Company and our customers.”
The attacker wants $50 million.
The company won’t pay because it feels “complying would not guarantee that the obtained information is deleted or that its misuse is prevented.”
Investigations into the incident continue, with GMO warning that 26,739 VDI servers may have been hit by the attack, and that users’ personal devices may be at risk.
The company is offering all users a ¥5,000 ($32) condolence payment and promised to make good on any trading losses caused by the attack.

This incident may have quite a blast radius, as GMO has warned that some trading apps may keep sessions alive even after passwords change. “Check your securities or FX company's guidance or your account page, and either disconnect all active sessions or ask the company's support desk to disconnect them,” GMO advised.
That ¥5,000 isn’t going to get anywhere near paying for the work customers will do to sort this out.
GMO CEO Masatoshi Kumagai acknowledged that in a blog post in which he described the payment as “a token of our initial sincerity towards our customers who have experienced inconvenience and worry.”

“We will dedicate the full resources of our group to providing a free alternative environment for six months, fundamentally overhauling our system infrastructure, and conducting a thorough investigation into the cause and preventing recurrence with the help of external experts,” he added.
But he also admitted that GMO knew the service’s security could be improved.
“Our in-house white-hat hackers had previously pointed out areas for improvement to the team,” he wrote. “The team took these points to heart and was working on countermeasures.”

“However, while we proceeded cautiously, considering the impact on service availability and prioritizing other issues, our response lacked sufficient depth and speed, allowing the attackers to exploit the vulnerability. I deeply regret that, despite having professionals on staff, we failed to fully translate their expertise into effective defenses as an organization.”
The CEO also said GMO can’t secure itself without government help.

“I've been involved in this world for 31 years, since the dawn of the internet industry,” he wrote. “The cyberspace that I built with my colleagues, believing it would bring smiles to people's faces, is now on the verge of being completely destroyed by malicious actors.”

“The ease with which open weight AI models can be combined and spread into countless attack tools has transformed cyberattacks, which once required advanced skills, into an era where anyone can easily carry them out,” he added, before claiming that GMO Group’s cybersecurity operation “has confirmed that the source of an unauthorized access attack targeting approximately 20 Japanese companies was the misuse of ‘ARTEX,’ an autonomous AI penetration testing tool originally intended for defense.”
Kumagai thinks public/private partnerships are needed to improve infosec across Japan.
“Yesterday, we submitted a proposal to the government to ‘apply proactive cyber defense,’” he wrote.

“We are by no means trying to shift the blame for our company's actions onto the government and beg for a bailout,” he wrote, but argued that unless Japan implements national-level defenses, more such incidents are unavoidable. ®

articles.headline: iPhone Lockdown Mode: The pros and cons of enabling Apple's security feature
keyFacts: Apple designed Lockdown Mode as an extreme security feature to protect high-risk individuals, such as journalists and politicians, from commercial spyware.
Lockdown Mode significantly improves device security by blocking everyday features like most message attachments, FaceTime calls, and certain browser functions.
Apple stated that the feature is unnecessary for most users because standard Apple devices already include built-in privacy protections.
body: iPhone Lockdown Mode: The pros and cons of enabling Apple's security feature
Lockdown Mode makes your iPhone much more secure against spyware, but most people don't need to use it.

The iPhone's Lockdown Mode has been around since 2022, but you might not have heard about it, let alone used it. It's one of those features that's well-hidden in the Settings app, plus it's not really meant for the average person. Apple itself calls the tool an "extreme" layer of security for the few people who may be targeted by commercial spyware such as NSO's Pegasus. Journalists, activists and politicians are among the potential targets of such spyware.

Anyone with an iPhone running iOS 16 or newer can try out Lockdown Mode. It's also available on iPadOS 16 and later, watchOS 10 and newer, and macOS 13 Ventura and later. To turn it on, open Settings and go to Privacy & Security. Scroll down until you find Lockdown Mode, then tap Turn On & Restart and confirm with your passcode. It's simple as that, and you'll find the option to disable it in the same place.
What Lockdown Mode disables on your iPhone

What makes Lockdown Mode strong is how it blocks many of the iPhone's features when enabled. However, many of those features are ones you likely use every day. In Messages, most kinds of attachments are blocked. Even link previews stop working, since they can serve as a backdoor for spyware. Lockdown Mode also restricts how JavaScript works in browsers, which may cause some websites to load slowly or not work at all. FaceTime calls are also blocked; only people you've called recently can reach you.

Your iPhone's connectivity is also limited when Lockdown Mode is on. For instance, wired connections are disabled when the device is locked — meaning it cannot communicate with a computer or accessory without your passcode. For wireless connectivity, your iPhone will no longer automatically connect to unsecured networks, and support for 2G and 3G networks is completely disabled (though these networks were discontinued in the US years ago).

You also can't install configuration profiles, which isn't ideal if your school or employer requires one. If you have an Apple Watch, phone call notifications from your iPhone won't show up on it. You'll see reduced functionality across other Apple services too: Home invitations and Game Center are not available, and photo sharing is restricted.
Who should leave Lockdown Mode on?

If Lockdown Mode sounds aggressive, it's because that's exactly what it was designed for. Back in 2023, an exploit known as "Blastpass" used iMessage to install the Pegasus spyware on Apple devices. However, researchers found that devices in Lockdown Mode were completely immune to the spyware. Apple offers a 100 percent bonus on top of the regular reward through its Security Bounty program to anyone who finds a way to bypass the feature, which shows how much the company trusts it. By restricting your iPhone to avoid potential attack vectors, you're given maximum security in exchange for reduced functionality and convenience.

The feature offers some flexibility: you can exclude certain contacts from messaging restrictions so your family can still send you videos or documents. You also have the option to exclude certain websites and apps from the feature. However, loosening these restrictions makes your device a little more vulnerable to attacks. If you think you're a target, it's best to keep all the default protections turned on.

For most people, there's no need to use Lockdown Mode. Apple devices already have many security and privacy features built in. Spyware like Pegasus usually targets public figures and is often deployed by governments that want to spy on opponents or protesters. If that's the case for you, it's definitely worth turning on Lockdown Mode — Apple may even send you a notification if it believes you've been targeted by spyware. If you're curious, try using Lockdown Mode for a few days to see what it's like. Chances are that the inconveniences it creates are not worth the extreme level of protection that few people need.
