Here are some other factoids:
- 7 incremental games, including 10 Million Pixels and Unharvest
- 15 lighthearted or comedic co-op games (aka friendslop) including Dude, Trust Me, Oar'Some Adventures, and Banana Airways
- 3 survival games including Frostrail, Never Be Alone and Arctic Drive
- 3 games that self-describe as "cozy" including Loftia
- 1 MMO in ArchAge Chronicles
- 1 haystack slop game
Among all 50 of these games, the only entry published by a traditional "blockbuster" publisher was Tropico 7, a Ubisoft affair [Oops, it's actually a Kalypso Media affair].
Teach My Little Sister How To Drive was one of the four games with AI disclosures. It leans heavily on an LLM-powered NPC which apparently cost its developer over $1,000 a day.

I'm not super surprised by the list, which you can find here, and which is topped by 1-6 player "asymmetric party game" Worst Class Ever. I'm not surprised because it really does capture the zeitgeist, but it's nevertheless pretty eye-opening when you compare it to the kinds of games that dominated the event only five years ago. For example, this Reddit thread lists highlights like Norco, Death Trash, Sable, Unpacking and The Inheritance of Crimson Manor, all of which people still talk about and play (though I am still waiting for Death Trash to enter 1.0).

It's hard not to see the outsize influence of Roblox and UGC in general on this list, which can sometimes be unappreciated by people who like to pay for games on Steam and read about them on PC Gamer. It's possible that the kids who were reared on cheap smartphone software are responsible for the surge in freewheeling online co-op games with simple graphics, but whatever the case, 2026 feels very, very different to 2021.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Shaun Prescott is the Australian editor of PC Gamer. With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. He thinks Lulu by Metallica and Lou Reed is an all-time classic that will receive its due critical reappraisal one day.

articles.headline: The Hitchhiker's Guide to why removing Ilhan Omar from Congress could be harder than Trump expects
keyFacts: President Trump and the Department of Justice are questioning Rep. Ilhan Omar over her legal name and immigration status.
Rep. Morgan Griffith stated that the House has the constitutional authority to expel members under extraordinary circumstances.
Legal precedents make removing or refusing to seat Rep. Omar difficult without ironclad proof of wrongdoing.
body: Republicans hope there are lots of Democrats who won’t win re-election next week and return to Capitol Hill. Republicans are imploring voters to kick them out.

But President Trump is focused on bouncing one Democrat from Congress who likely wins re-election in a solidly blue district. That’s Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.). She carried her district two years ago with nearly three-quarters of the vote. But President Trump questions whether Omar is in the country legally and, therefore, qualified to sit in Congress.
"She used a fake name to be sworn in," said the President. "She's a little troublemaker."

The Department of Justice is investigating Omar for potential immigration fraud. Federal authorities raided her Washington, DC home recently and removed 17 items. That included phones, notebooks, a camera and a Somali phrase book for her kids.
President Trump suggests that her name is not "Ilhan Omar" and that it’s "an entirely different name name. Ihan Nur Sayeed Elmi. It's close."
A federal filing in that inquiry lists the Congresswoman’s name as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar."
That’s why the President says "she must immediately resign from Congress."
A reporter for Fox Digital confronted the Congresswoman about her name.
SOMALI RAP PROMISING TO 'SCATTER' ENEMIES UNDERSCORES OMAR'S SERENE LAKESIDE VIDEO
"Is your name Ilhan Sayed, Ilhan Nur Sayed Alami, or Ilhan Abdullahi Omar?" asked Rashid Umar Abbasi, working for Fox.
"Ilhan Abdullahi Omar. You know it," replied Omar.
"Ma'am?" asked Abbasi for clarification.
"It's Ilhan Abdullahi Omar," she confirmed.

The Clerk of the House of Representatives officially lists the Congresswoman as solely "Ilhan Omar" on 15 different financial disclosure reports dating back to 2018. That’s even before she entered Congress. The same with the Minnesota state legislature where Omar served prior to coming to Washington.
The discrepancy is why the President wants the House to banish Omar.
"She will not be legally allowed to be a member of that august body that sits in Washington," said President Trump.
But it’s not his call.
However, Article I, Section 5 of the Constitution grants both bodies of Congress final authority about who it admits to its membership.
At least one House Republican is willing to explore that. But only if the facts merit it.
"The House has the prerogative to seat or not seat and to throw Members out if it so chooses," said Rep. Morgan Griffith (R-Va.). "There ought to be good sound reasons for it."
It’s a different set of rules, but Griffith had experience with this as the Virginia House of Delegates grappled with a similar issue about seating lawmakers in the Commonwealth in 1988.
But Congress is altogether different.
"It would be extraordinary. And it should be extraordinary and it should not be used except in extraordinary circumstances," said Griffith.
Yours truly asked what would meet that bar to block someone from serving in the House.
"It's like the Supreme Court said about pornography. I'll know it when I see it," said Griffith, paraphrasing late Justice Potter Stewart from a key 1964 obscenity case.
ILHAN OMAR HIT WITH EXPULSION THREAT AS GOP LAWMAKER VOWS TO BOOT HER FROM CONGRESS OVER DOJ PROBE

House Republicans have two options to deal with Omar if they are truly determined to take action – regardless of what is proven or not. Qualifications for the House are pretty simple. You must be a citizen and a resident of the state you are representing. And, you must be 25 years old. You could even be convicted of a crime and serving time in jail. The Constitution is silent on all other credentials. You could also have a resume which is without a blemish. It doesn’t matter. The House could still take action against you.

The first conceivable option could come now. The Constitution grants the House and Senate the right to expel Members – provided there’s a two-thirds vote. Any scenario to expel Omar seems remarkable. Especially since she hasn’t been convicted of a crime. And even if she is charged, there are lots of other issues which could emerge before a trial.

It would be strange to have the executive branch of government trying to remove a Member of the legislative branch of government. Moreover, it’s likely that the House counsel would contest any effort by federal prosecutors to procure Omar’s official House communication devices as well as documents. There’s a firewall between the legislative branch and executive branch known as the "Speech or Debate Clause." Article I, Section 6 of the Constitution grants lawmakers privileges tied to their official duties. So getting those papers — let alone potentially deporting her as some have suggested – is a far cry. Especially since she’s a Member and this all hinges on expulsion.

Moreover, two-thirds of the House will never vote to expel a Member under these circumstances unless there’s ironclad proof of wrongdoing. That’s why the House has only expelled six Members in its history. The last was former Rep. George Santos (R-N.Y.) in 2023.
However, what may be an issue is whether or not there could be an objection to seating Omar when the new Congress convenes in January.

In 1968, then Rep. Adam Clayton Powell (D-NY) faced a criminal investigation. House Speaker John McCormack (D-Mass.) refused to seat Powell – even though he met all other requirements. The Supreme Court ruled in Powell v. McCormack that the House can’t exclude a Member if they meet the basic standards to serve in the House.
TRUMP IMMIGRATION WIN COULD STRENGTHEN ADMIN'S HAND IN LOOMING SUPREME COURT FIGHT

That said, it’s possible there could be motions not to seat Omar – or even other progressive Members-elect who have said controversial things about the U.S. and Constitution. Such a motion would come right after the House chooses a Speaker. But the Speaker has not sworn-in the rest of the Members. The House would then swear-in everyone – except the Member or Members-elect who may face questions about serving. Once the House swears in the rest of the body, it can then vote on a motion not to expel those persons, table the motion, or refer the motion to a committee for investigation.

In 1985, the House did not swear-in Rep. Frank McCloskey (D-Ind.) and decided to investigate whether or not he won his seat in the Hoosier State. The House didn’t swear-in McCloskey for several months.
Based on Powell v. McCormack , it’s hard to envision a scenario where the House declines to seat someone. But it might not do it immediately based on the McCloskey case.

Of course, it’s always probable that the House could seat someone – and then expel them. That doesn’t collide headlong with the Powell decision. But considering that the House has only expelled six members, those circumstances are doubtful, too.
What’s in a name? Especially for Ilhan Omar. Her adversaries may raise questions about her name. But it’s doubtful they can do anything about her position.

articles.headline: Rivian Halloween Update Turns R1, R2 Into Ghostbusting EVs Through Nov. 2
keyFacts: Rivian released a Ghostbusters-themed Halloween over-the-air update for its R1 and R2 electric vehicles developed with Sony Pictures.
The seasonal software update features themed exterior lights, audio tracks, dashboard displays, an arcade game, and a voice control tie-in available through November 2.
Rivian also built physical Ecto-1 homages based on the R1S to display at select retail locations.
body: Halloween is one of my family’s favorite holidays, a sentiment clearly shared by somebody at Rivian. Every October, owners of its electric trucks and SUVs can activate Halloween Mode, which changes the exterior lights, sounds and graphics on the infotainment display to match the spookiest season. It’s pretty fun.

This year, Halloween Mode on the R1S, R1T and R2 EVs has become a Ghostbusters–themed experience that Rivian says changes each of its EVs “into a ghost-hunting machine.” The over-the-air update adds lights and sounds, easter eggs and hidden clues in the digital infotainment system, a tie-in with the Rivian Assistant voice control system, and an arcade-style Halloween game that can be played while parked.
The update, developed in collaboration with Sony Pictures, is available now and runs through Nov. 2.
More from CNET
Who ya gonna call?

A new in-vehicle Ghostbusters app bundles the seasonal features into a single red toggle, accessible while parked. Tapping it syncs the EV’s interior and exterior lighting and themed audio to match the Ghostbusters’ car, the Specialized Electronical Vehicular Device (or Ecto-1). Second-generation R1 and R2 owners can also choose from Proton Pack, Slimer, Ghost Trap, or Peter Venkman themes. R1 Gen 1 owners only get the main Ecto-1 theme, but each option pairs a unique exterior LED sequence with a matching audio track. The EV can also be set to automatically trigger a random themed light-and-sound show whenever someone walks past, giving trick-or-treaters a fun surprise.

Inside, the dashboard and rear displays transform to match Ecto-1’s control panels, playing a version of the iconic Ray Parker Jr. Ghostbusters theme song. The Rivian mobile and smartwatch apps also update to match the vehicle’s controls, allowing owners to trigger Ecto-1’s siren and flashing lights from outside the vehicle.

In addition to putting on a show for passersby, the spooky infotainment mode features clues hidden throughout the EV’s menus that can be tapped to reveal secret characters — like Slimer and Rivian’s Ghost Guard — triggering animations, audio and easter eggs. Even the Rivian Assistant voice command system gets in on the act, taking on an eerie tone for the season, triggering light shows with spoken commands, reading clues for the in-dash scavenger hunt and playing sound effects on request.

Rounding out the update is Mallow Mash, an arcade game accessible from the main touchscreen where players race against the clock to pop mini Stay Puft Marshmallow Men. The full creature feature set — including the scavenger hunt, the arcade game and most of the lights and sounds — is only available when the vehicle is in park. However, the touchscreen’s visual theme will remain active if switched before driving, so you can take the show on the road.

To get in on the fun, both the vehicle software and the Rivian mobile app need to be up to date. Once updated, look for a prompt on the driver display that asks whether you’d like to “hunt some ghosts” and opens the Ghostbusters app.
The real Ecto-R1

In addition to the seasonal software, Rivian also built a few physical homages to the original Ecto-1 based on its R1S. Dubbed the Ecto-R1, the full-size electric SUV features white paint on the body and 22-inch Aero wheels, red graphics running the length of the chassis, and the No-Ghost logo on its hood and front doors. Rivian has loaded the EV’s roof rack with a custom frame filled with screen-accurate sirens, spotlights, a radar dish and side tanks, as well as vintage emergency lights sourced and restored to complete the look. It’s so cool.

I couldn’t convince Rivian to sell me one of its custom Ecto-R1s — though that hasn’t stopped me from asking repeatedly — but the builds will be on display for fans to check out in person at Rivian retail spaces in Austin, Miami, San Francisco, New York, and Laguna Beach and Venice, California. The full list of events is on Rivian’s Halloween page.

articles.headline: From forgettable EFL loans to Ballon d'Or winner - Kane's 'Cinderella story'
keyFacts: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or, becoming the first Englishman to claim the award in 25 years.
Former manager Tim Sherwood described Kane's rise from difficult early loan spells to world-class status as a Cinderella story.
Sherwood suggested that Kane might eventually return to the Premier League in the future to target the all-time scoring record.
body: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player

Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or to become first Englishman to land award in 25 years; Bayern Munich and England captain's Ballon d'Or victory called 'Cinderella story' by Tim Sherwood; watch Bayern vs Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, kick-off 5.30pm
Monday 26 October 2026 23:50, UK
From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.
"This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports.
"He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking, 'Are we talking about the same kid?'
"There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further.
"I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest."
The Bayern Munich striker has become the first English Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years and just the fifth in its history.
The last English winner, Michael Owen, had a simpler route to the top, winning it aged 22 in 2001, just four years after his senior debut at Liverpool.
Kane's win has come at the age of 33, some 15 years after his senior debut on loan at Leyton Orient in League One.
"I think we have to highlight his journey," says Sherwood, who Kane thanked on stage when collecting the Ballon d'Or.
"Even when we go back to Michael (Owen), he was a superstar as a kid, and he got the opportunities at a very young age at Liverpool, which is a giant football club.
"Kane came through the hard way, really. He was a player who wasn't universally loved.
"He's not like a Max Dowman, for instance, who is a superstar at 16 years of age.
"He (Kane) struggled to get some game time and to get a manager to really, really buy into what he had."
Kane even mentioned his tough path to the top in his Ballon d'Or acceptance speech.
He said: "My journey wasn't straightforward; I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now."
For Sherwood, it was those low-key loan spells at Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester that have turned Kane into the world's top player.
"I hear a lot of people talking about failed loans," he says, "but we never felt like that because we felt that him playing in U21 football was a waste of time.
"They were really good loans, and those loans were the reason why we've got a player like that."
Kane's 'sliding doors' moment
Kane was out in the cold at Spurs until Andre Villas-Boas' sacking, when Sherwood's subsequent arrival opened the door.
He handed Kane his first-ever Premier League start - and the then-20-year-old took his chance as he scored the opener in a 5-1 home win over Sunderland in April 2014.

"He wasn't getting anywhere unfortunately," Sherwood says. "He wasn't around the first-team squad, so I suppose it's a sliding doors moment that I managed to take over until the end of the season and I managed to give him a stage where he could perform."
And perform he has.

Kane has hit nearly 550 goals for club and country to become Tottenham's record scorer, England's all-time scorer, England's leading World Cup scorer and the top English scorer in Champions League history.
His incredible goalscoring feats hit new heights last season as he plundered 73 goals in all competitions.

Sixty-one of those came for Bayern in all competitions, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues last season. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.
For Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher, Kane's £100m move from Spurs to Bayern in the summer of 2023 has allowed him global recognition and respect.
"It's a move he needed to make," Carragher tells Sky Sports.
"I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one.
"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.
"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."
'Kane is an example to all young kids'
The Bayern move has delivered the trophies Kane so desperately craved.
Despite winning three Premier League Golden Boots at Spurs and becoming their all-time top scorer, personal honours were never the aim of the game for Kane, according to Sherwood.
His trophyless career at N17 is what drove Kane to join Bayern, where he has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a German Cup.
"The boy loves Tottenham," Sherwood says. "He wanted to win there, but he was winning individual accolades at Spurs, and it wasn't enough for him.

"When we all grow up, we all want to be footballers, and we don't want to be footballers because we want to be rich. There are possibly some players like that now, but that certainly wasn't his motivation.
"He wanted to go to a team that could win, and he picked Bayern, and we have to say it's been a good choice."
Sherwood adds: "He's a 100 per cent team man. If I told you he would rather win the Champions League and the Bundesliga title than the Ballon d'Or for himself, that would be the truth.
"Not every player would say that, but I genuinely believe that that is the measure of the man and that's what you're talking about, and that's why he's such a dream to manage.
"The work rate and the example he shows to any young kids coming through, and to genuinely go around the houses to try and make it, and he certainly made it."
Is Kane England's greatest-ever player?
Kane continues to break record after record in Germany.
He is the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, has the most goals in his first 100 Bundesliga appearances and is the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goal contributions.
It is that last stat where Kane has proven he is more than just a goal scorer. His excellent vision, awareness and superb passing range make him an exquisite playmaker.

This was on show recently in Bayern's 2-2 Champions League home draw against Arsenal as Kane, who spent much of the game dropping deep, sumptuously set up Alphonso Davies for an equaliser with a pinpoint ball from inside the centre circle.
His assist ability has been on display for years, where at Spurs he claimed the Premier League Playmaker of the Season award in the 2020/21 campaign.
So, does his all-round game combined with his records and this Ballon d'Or prize make him England's greatest-ever player? Not for Carragher, who puts a fellow English Ballon d'Or winner ahead of him.
"I would still always put Bobby Charlton as the greatest England player ever," he says.
"He's won the World Cup. He's won the Champions League with Manchester United. As a midfield player, he was the leading goalscorer for a very long time for both United and England.

"I'd still always say Bobby Charlton, because right now this England team, even though it's been a golden period for us, Harry Kane and the others still haven't got their hands on a trophy, and that's what Bobby Charlton did."
Could Kane return to Spurs?
Kane, who needs just one cap to become England's most-capped player, and although there are plenty of trophies to be won, Sherwood believes there is a longer-term goal in Kane's thinking.
"I believe he will come back for that individual accolade to be the Premier League top scorer in the future, maybe in a couple of years' time," the ex-Premier League-winning captain says.
Kane is 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's all-time Premier League record of 260 goals.
"He will only come back to a team he believes can win," says Sherwood. "At the moment you're looking at Man City with the troubles they've got, so Liverpool possibly, that could be a chance for him.
"Tottenham could be in the frame if they start progressing. Manchester United could be in the frame, but they've got a long way to go to prove that they can win anything as well.
"I'm not sure it's ever going to be Chelsea or Arsenal because of the Tottenham connection.

"So, it's on a positive note for Tottenham fans if they can start progressing and you can prove to him that he can come back and he can possibly have a good chance of winning at your club as he will have at Liverpool, Man Utd and Man City - but we don't know what's going to happen with them - then there's an opportunity he might come back and see out his career where he started it."
It seems a fitting final chapter in Kane's Cinderella story.

articles.headline: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
keyFacts: OpenAI announced three major AI discoveries in math, computer science, and physics.
External experts are guiding or examining the computer science and physics results, while math output was released directly.
OpenAI released an open letter seeking community input on norms for handling AI-generated breakthroughs.
body: Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more “major” discoveries in math, computer science, and physics. What’s different this time is the choice to have external experts that OpenAI describes as “shepherds” guiding the results in computer science and physics, while for the math problem it says that they advised it to release the AI output for researchers to work through their own explanations.
OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
This time OpenAI says it’s taking new advice from scientists on how to release the results.

Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation. The proof uses an auxiliary partial differential equation to establish Sogge’s local smoothing for waves in every spatial dimension at least two. It also yields the Kakeya maximal and dimension conjectures and Stein’s spherical restriction estimates throughout the interior of the conjectured range. We are releasing the model output directly, as we did in our October 6 release.

The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False. The paper gives a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space. The case of 3-SAT refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. An independent working group of computer scientists led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams will examine and explain the proof. At the group’s request, we are making the materials public immediately so others can examine them as well.

This approach could have its own issues, the company admits, and the AGMAI panel of math advisers OpenAI put together just said yesterday that “we recommend that AI companies do not adopt” the practices of designating certain people to receive the output first, citing unequal access, borrowed reputation, and biased selection as a few of the issues. Instead, they recommended that in the future, AI labs release output on scholarly repositories, with Lean-formalized proofs, info on how the problems were chosen, funding for people working on understanding the results, and other information.

The physics information has not been released in full, but is a “mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics.” According to OpenAI, “David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.”

The computer science collaboration is said to prove that the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), which has been widely believed to be true, is actually false. OpenAI says verification of the result will be guided by a group of three experts that includes UC San Diego’s Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who were part of the group that originally proposed it in 1999, as well as MIT professor Ryan Williams. The group decided to release the AI output write-up and Lean proof on GitHub today.
They also released an open letter to the community asking for input on how to examine the claim, and about setting norms for dealing with AI-generated breakthroughs:
We would welcome discussion of three broader questions:
What expectations should govern early access to AI-generated results, disclosure of conflicts of interest, and the use of unpublished material for subsequent research?
How should credit recognize both new discoveries and the work of checking, fixing, simplifying, explaining, and extending them?
How can we support students and researchers as methods and research directions change, while preserving the understanding and judgment needed to question results and develop new ideas?

There’s similar documentation for the math breakthrough, where its model “produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture in all dimensions.” Just a few months ago, NYU professor Hong Wang was awarded a prestigious Fields Medal by the International Mathematical Union for resolving the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions.

articles.headline: London City's Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or
keyFacts: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time.
Putellas captained Barcelona to a quadruple in the 2025-26 season before joining London City Lionesses in July.
England captain Harry Kane also won the men's Ballon d'Or, becoming the first English player to win it since 2001.
body: - Published
Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time, keeping the prize in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year.
Putellas, 32, captained Barcelona to Champions League glory as part of a quadruple in 2025-26, before joining Women's Super League (WSL) side London City Lionesses in July.
She joins Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati on three Ballon d'Or Feminin crowns - her former Barcelona colleague won the award in 2023, 2024 and 2025 after Putellas did so in 2021 and 2022.
The past six Ballons d'Or have been won by the Spanish pair, with Norway's Ada Hegerberg (2018) and Megan Rapinoe of the United States (2019) the only non-Spaniards to claim the prize.
Putellas' latest victory caps a remarkable return to the pinnacle of world football after suffering a career-threatening anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in 2022.
"All the boys and girls around the world - if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn't matter if you're a boy or if you're a girl," Putellas said.
"Doesn't matter where you come from. Don't listen if someone tells you, you can't do it. Believe in yourself."

She collected the most votes from an international panel of journalists across Fifa's top-50 ranked countries, with Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor coming second and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw third.
Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or, becoming the first English player to do so since Michael Owen in 2001.
The numbers don't lie
While Barcelona are always overwhelming favourites to win the three competitions on offer in Spain, Putellas' performances last season showed that she is still among the world's elite.

Nicknamed 'La Reina' - meaning the queen - Putellas scored 21 goals and provided 13 assists in all competitions, ranking her third and second respectively among players across Europe's top five leagues.
Seven of those goals came in the Women's Champions League as Barcelona claimed a fourth continental title in six seasons.
Only Pernille Harder (eight), Alessia Russo (nine) and Ewa Pajor (11) scored more, all of whom are strikers by trade.
But Putellas' contributions to Barcelona's attacking play went far beyond scoring goals herself.
In Liga F - which Barcelona won for a seventh consecutive season - she finished joint-sixth for assists (seven) and fourth for open-play chances created (40).
Across Europe's top five leagues, only Claudia Pina (199), Vicky Lopez (183) and Georgia Stanway (168) recorded more sequence involvements ending in an open-play shot than Putellas (151).

In all competitions, she created more chances (89, 19 of which were big chances) and completed more passes ending in the final third (965) than any other player in Liga F, the Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de Espana.

Only Bayern Munich's Klara Buhl created as many chances as Putellas in the Champions League last season (36), the most by a player in a single edition of the competition since Caroline Graham Hansen in 2021-22 (38).
From watching Iniesta to winning it all
Putellas was born and grew up in the Catalan municipality of Mollet del Valles, about 12 miles north-east of Barcelona.
She began playing football in the street, and soon became a Barcelona fan and a regular attendee at Camp Nou.
With matches always on the TV at home, former Spain and Barcelona star Andres Iniesta and Brazilian duo Rivaldo and Ronaldinho quickly became her idols.
After attending a summer football camp run by Xavi and playing for local side CE Sabadell, Putellas spent a year at La Masia, Barcelona's famous youth academy.
Spells at Espanyol and Levante followed the disbandment of her girls team, before she eventually returned to Barca in 2012.
Cue the start of a 14-year career with her childhood club during which she won 38 trophies, including 10 league titles and four European cups.

But after winning the Ballon d'Or for the first time in 2021, one of the toughest moments of Putellas' career came when she suffered an ACL injury on the eve of Euro 2022, ruling her out of the tournament.
Though she retained the Ballon d'Or later that year, it took a while for her to return to her best level. Playing only a bit-part role in Spain's triumphant 2023 World Cup campaign would have stung.

After scoring in the 2024 Champions League final and improving further the following season, in 2025-26 she shouldered much of Barcelona's creative burden as Aitana Bonmati missed five months through injury and ended the season a quadruple winner.
If that was not enough, the midfielder scored twice in a 4-0 thrashing of England in June that secured Spain's place at the 2027 World Cup at the Lionesses' expense.
With her contract at Barcelona expiring and keen for a fresh challenge, Putellas made the decision to leave her childhood club. She, and her fans, were distraught.
She had several offers from England, Mexico and the United States, but joined the ambitious project of US billionaire Michelle Kang at London City Lionesses in July.

"I'm just always looking forward to better things and that's why I'm here too, because I always need to be moving as a person and a player," Putellas told BBC's Women's Football Weekly podcast in August.
With three goals and one assist in seven WSL games for her new club, it is clear Putellas is still deserving of her nickname.

articles.headline: Skydance Institutes Company-Wide Mandatory Return To Office So It Can Avoid Saying ‘Layoffs’ So Soon After Merger
keyFacts: Skydance instituted a mandatory five-day return-to-office policy across its company divisions, according to a report by Vertical Slice.
The policy affects Skydance Games, DC Comics, and other media holdings, alongside a voluntary buyout program designed to reduce staff headcount.
The restructuring follows the completion of an 110 billion dollar merger between Paramount and Warner Bros earlier this month.
body: Tale as old as time. Big company completes a huge buyout for billions of dollars, employees get laid off swiftly after. Only Skydance is getting “creative” to avoid having “layoffs” in the headlines. Vertical Slice reports that employees at Skydance Games, the amalgamation of what was once WB Games and Paramount Games, have received a mandatory five-day return to office (RTO) notice.

The RTO policy is business-wide, affecting Skydance’s games division, DC Comics, and its numerous other media holdings. In addition to mandatory RTO, which can often be corporate-speak for “we want layoffs without the bad press or severance payouts,” Skydance is also setting up a voluntary buyout program that’ll help reduce headcount.

WB Games has already faced a number of reductions before this latest soft-layoff. Last year, WB Games shut down Monolith Productions which had been working on a Wonder Woman game, along with MultiVerus studio Player First Games and mobile development studio Warner Bros. San Diego. WB said the restructuring was to shift focus to its core game franchises including Harry Potter and Mortal Kombat, but WB Games’ overall value was apparently so minute that Netflix didn’t factor in its worth when the streamer was trying to outbid Paramount Skydance for the whole Warner Bros. kit and kaboodle last year. Paramount and Warner Bros. completed their merger, coming together under the name Skydance earlier this month to the tune of $110 billion.

articles.headline: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or as he beats Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to ultimate prize
keyFacts: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or at an award ceremony in London, becoming the first Englishman to claim the trophy in 25 years.
Kane beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal for the prize after scoring 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England during the 2025/26 season.
During the ceremony, Alexia Putellas won the Women’s Ballon d’Or and several other awards were distributed to players, coaches, and clubs.
body: Harry Kane has won the Ballon d’Or at the award ceremony in London on Monday evening.
The Bayern Munich superstar has become the first Englishman to win the prestigious trophy in 25 years.
Kane is the fifth Englishman to be crowned the world’s best player with Michael Owen, Kevin Keegan, Bobby Charlton and Stanley Matthews coming before him Getty
Michael Owen was the last England international to claim the award in 2001, with Kane joining him in the history books.

“I’m almost speechless. (Luckily) I have this list here,” Kane said upon receiving the award. “Thank you to France Football, to the Ballon d’Or for putting on this amazing event. Being here in London has made it extra special. It looked like a good omen for me tonight so thank you very much.

“Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was really tough this year, some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my teammates, some world-class players in the room tonight.”

Kane went on to thank his Bayern Munich teammates as well as manager Vincent Kompany, continuing: “The way you guys push me, the way we compete, me against (Dayot Upamecano) in training every week, it makes me a better player, makes me want to improve.
“To Vinny (Kompany), I think he’s at home or still in the hospital — wishing you very well and hope this has given you a bit of energy.”
And the club where it all began for him and where he became a legend, Tottenham, also got a shoutout.
He said: “I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur . I wouldn’t be where I am today without Tottenham.
“I was there from when I was 11 and the club and all the coaches helped me to live my dreams and all of those memories and those ups and downs have led me to where I am today.”
Kane finished by saying: “It’s an honour to play for Bayern Munich. To represent you is a real privilege and I’m glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich for sure.
“To all of my England teammates — Bukayo (Saka) is here tonight representing England — again the same. We had a special year. It wasn’t the perfect year but we had a lot of good moments.
Kane scored six goals at the World Cup and has 91 goals for England overall AFP
“We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness, the way we trained, the way we played, the togetherness in the hotel at the World Cup.
“It was truly an honour to captain you, lead you, it makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us.”
Kane’s magical 2026
The 33-year-old scored a stunning 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England combined during the 2025/26 season.
He won the Bundesliga title at club level, breaking endless records as well as lifting the German Cup and German Super Cup, while also captaining the Three Lions to the World Cup semi-finals .
54 goals from his incredible tally have come in 2026 alone, along with 13 assists in all competitions for Bayern.
Mbappe and Yamal miss out
Second-placed Mbappe missed out on a career-first Ballon d’Or despite scoring 58 goals in 60 games in the 2025/26 season.
The Real Madrid superstar also won the Golden Boot at the World Cup this summer as France reached the semi-finals, becoming the tournament’s all-time top scorer .
He didn’t win a single trophy last term, and has been beaten by Kane at the ceremony.

At 19 years old, Yamal could have become the youngest winner of the Ballon d’Or ever after winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, although he did claim get a consolation prize in his third successive Kopa Trophy.
Yamal won the La Liga title and Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona , scoring 25 goals and providing 20 assist in 2025/26.
His success with La Roja on the international stage in the USA did not give him the edge over his competitors.
2026 Ballon d’Or awards winners
There were a series of other awards handed out during the ceremony with Alexia Putellas winning the Women’s Ballon d’Or prize, this being her third crown.
Putellas won the Women’s Ballon d’Or for the third time AFP
Kane’s England teammate Bukayo Saka claimed the Socrates Award, a prize given to players for their humanitarian work Getty
Kane also won the Gerd Muller Trophy, the award given for the best men’s striker in the game, with Mexico’s Charlyn Corral winning the female equivalent.

The first award of the night was given to Yamal, who won the Men’s Young Talent of the Year prize for a third year running. Fellow Spaniard and Barcelona star Vicky Lopez won Women’s Young Talent of the Year.
There was more sweeping success for Spain with Unai Simon winning the Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year award and compatriot Cata Coll named Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year.
It was Spanish glory with the coach awards too; Spain men’s boss Luis De La Fuente and Barcelona women’s manager Pere Romeu emerging victorious.
Barcelona won the Women’s Club of the Year but the Men’s Club of the Year was given to Paris Saint-Germain having retained their European crown for a second season running.
There was another English winner in Arsenal star Bukayo Saka, who claimed the Socrates Award for his work with the BigShoe charity, which funds medical surgeries for children.
Ballon d'Or awards winners
Men’s Ballon d’Or – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/England)
Women’s Ballon d’Or – Alexia Putellas (London City Lionesses/Spain)
Men’s Young Talent of the Year – Lamine Yamal (Barcelona/Spain)
Women’s Young Talent of the Year – Vicky Lopez (Barcelona/Spain)
Men’s Coach of the Year – Luis De La Fuente (Spain)
Women’s Coach of the Year – Pere Romeu (Barcelona/Spain)
Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year – Cata Coll (Barcelona/Spain)
Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year – Unai Simon (Athletic Bilbao/Spain)
Socrates Award – Bukayo Saka (Arsenal/England)
Women’s Club of the Year – Barcelona
Men’s Club of the Year – Paris Saint-Germain
Women’s Striker of the Year – Charlyn Corral (Pachuda/Mexico)
Men’s Striker of the Year – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/England)

articles.headline: Trump’s vicious closing message in Michigan
keyFacts: At a Michigan rally, Donald Trump called Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed a jihadist who should not enter the Capitol.
The remarks come as El-Sayed leads in most recent polls against Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers in Michigan.
Trump's upcoming itinerary before the election includes rallies in Mississippi, Texas, Ohio, South Carolina, and Florida.
body: The day after former President Barack Obama and Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed campaigned together in Detroit, President Donald Trump launched an anti-Muslim attack against El-Sayed. | Emily Elconin/Bloomberg via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump’s midterm barnstorming is getting uglier and more desperate.

What’s happening? At a campaign rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, Trump launched a new round of anti-Muslim attacks against Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, describing him as a “jihadist” who “should never be allowed inside the halls of our great beautiful Capitol.”

“If Abdul and the Democrats win,” Trump told supporters , “they will open the floodgates and invite hordes of jihadists to our shores, creating a nightmare of violence and terror until you cannot even have a Christmas.”
What’s the context? Trump’s speech marks the crescendo — so far — of what has become an increasingly Islamophobic midterm campaign by the Republican Party, centered on El-Sayed.

Former Rep. Mike Rogers, Michigan’s Republican Senate nominee, has repeatedly tried to link El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, and Republicans have also attempted to wield Islamophobia against the Democratic Party as a whole.

On Sunday, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott told Fox News that his Democratic opponent, Gina Hinojosa, “supports Sharia law,” while at the Republican midterm convention in September, Texas Sen. Ted Cruz said that “communism” and “Islamism” were allying against Republicans.

What’s the big picture? In addition to his overt Islamophobia, Trump’s presence on the campaign trail in the final few weeks of the midterm elections has been decidedly strange and surprisingly heavy on physical descriptions of Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) .

Now, with just eight days to go, Trump’s itinerary features rallies in Mississippi, Texas, Ohio, South Carolina, and Florida — all Republican states where the party has found itself, to one degree or another, with a tougher-than-expected Senate race on its hands.
It’s hardly the travel schedule of a president who feels good about his party’s chances— such as in Michigan, where El-Sayed is leading in most recent polls .
And with that, it’s time to log off…

US elections may not be until next week, but two other countries held theirs over the weekend: Serbia and Brazil. As my colleague Caitlin Dewey reports in Vox’s Today, Explained newsletter , both resulted in surprise victories over right-wing nationalist parties, with Serbia ousting its incumbent strongman, Aleksandar Vučić.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory over Flávio Bolsonaro is also especially good news for the climate: As the New York Times reported earlier this month, the fate of the Amazon rainforest may well have hinged on the outcome of the election.
Thanks for reading, have a great evening, and we’ll see you tomorrow!

articles.headline: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
keyFacts: Microsoft announced voluntary buyout offers to about 60,000 employees, representing a quarter of its global workforce, according to CNBC.
Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said eligible organizations were selected based on business priorities, customer commitments, and workforce needs.
The voluntary exit offer is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
body: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company. CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce. The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft. While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.

Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Microsoft employees at level 70 or below will be eligible for the buyout program. The company's employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level. According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected "based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs."

The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026. In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees. In July, the Xbox division laid off 3,200 employees , or about 20 percent of its entire gaming division. As reported by CNBC , about 30 percent of eligible employees accepted the retirement offer, lessening the impact of the planned layoffs, according to Coleman. While the offer in April went out to long-tenured employees who might be nearing the end of their career, the VEO expands the effort to a much larger potential pool.

articles.headline: Mass Effect fans ramp up efforts to save BioWare's RPG series with a Times Square billboard and plans for more ads outside The Game Awards
keyFacts: Fans launched the Save Mass Effect movement after publisher EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next game in the series.
Organizers and content creator Kala Elizabeth placed a billboard in Times Square and plan further ads near EA offices and at The Game Awards.
Organizer Mer Mora stated that community crowdfunding will pay for the ads, with excess donations going to the Game Workers' Hardship Fund.
body: Fans continue to rally around the 'Save Mass Effect' movement, this time with a billboard at Times Square and more initiatives planned throughout the rest of the year.

Last week, publisher EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next Mass Effect game. In the days since, an increasingly loud community-organised campaign has attempted to make Electronic Arts reverse course and ensure that the beloved sci-fi universe can journey forward in some form.

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8
— We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) October 26, 2026

The We Are Mass Effect community group and content creator Kala Elizabeth are now collaborating on a number of initiatives, including a billboard at New York City's Times Square that points people toward the growing online "SaveMassEffect" hashtag. Text that reads "Kellah Si'yah" is sprawled across the ad - referencing the in-game ship that ferried different races to settle the Andromeda system.

"Apart from the Times Square billboard, we also have several other initiatives in the works. An advertising truck near EA's headquarters in Redwood City and in Edmonton, a mobile billboard for N7 Day, and another one in LA for The Game Awards. All of them will carry a message in support of #SaveMassEffect," one of the group's organisers, Mer Mora, told me via email.

The 'SaveMassEffect' petition gained a huge amount of traction this weekend with 226,000 signatures and counting. The petition urges rights holder EA to commit to "the continued development of Mass Effect" by either funding a new game in the series or by licensing it to an outside studio who can do it justice.

"All of these initiatives will be funded by the community itself! We're putting together a GoFundMe after receiving an overwhelming response from community members eager to contribute financially to make all of these happen," Mora added. "And given the incredible support and generosity we've received, any funds raised beyond our goal will be donated to the Game Workers' Hardship Fund, which supports game developers who have been laid off." The United Videogame Workers union (UVW-CWA) opened the fund earlier this year to support the many laid off video game workers across Canada and the USA.

articles.headline: ‘Stick A Fork In It’: Ex-Trump Official Says 1 Move Could Mark The End Of Trump Presidency
keyFacts: Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci warned that Donald Trump could face removal from office if he meets with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.
Scaramucci stated on a podcast that such a meeting aimed at ending the war in Ukraine without Volodymyr Zelenskyy would destroy the Republican Party.
Scaramucci predicted that disaffected Republicans would join Democrats in Congress to impeach and remove Trump from the presidency if the meeting occurs.
body: Anthony Scaramucci, who briefly served as Donald Trump’s communications director in his first term, has warned that the president could create serious trouble for himself — and his party — if he agrees to a proposed meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

“Trump should be very careful with that because he would probably — he’s going to push the envelope where he may be asked to leave the presidency,” said Scaramucci on Sunday’s episode of “The Daily Beast Podcast.”

The proposed meeting — which, per The Wall Street Journal, Putin floated in an Oct. 9 call with Trump — would bring the leaders together in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit next month.
The intended focus of the meeting, sources told the Journal, would be to negotiate an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine — but without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Asked about the proposed meeting outside the White House last week, Trump said he’s open to whatever he can do to end the war “whether somebody’s there or not” before suggesting that denuclearization would be the focus of the talks.
Scaramucci, joining the likes of the New York Post and The Wall Street Journal editorial boards, advised the president against attending such a meeting.
“If that meeting were to happen, then I would tell you that the Republican Party is completely dead; we’d probably have to get a tombstone out,” he began.

“And you tell me the date of that meeting and I will chisel into the tombstone: ‘This party got started in Wisconsin in 1856, it elected Abraham Lincoln in 1860, and it died on the date of that meeting.’ The party is dead — sticking a fork in it — the Cheney, Bush, Romney, Reagan, Eisenhower party dead, stick a fork in it.”

Addressing those who might doubt his presidency-ending prediction, Scaramucci insisted it’s “not crazy,” as he expects Democrats will take the House in the midterms and could find a two-thirds majority in the Senate to remove Trump from office.
“Let’s say they split and they go 50-50, you need 17 Republicans that have had enough of him,” Scaramucci said.

“They hate his guts... he hates them, by the way, and they hate him. And so, just so you know, keep pushing and keep doing this sort of nonsense that they all hate ... And you’re going to get cross traffic into Democrats who say, ‘Impeach him in the House, I’ll pull up 17 votes and we’ll knock him out of the presidency.’”
Trump has already been impeached twice in the House. However, the Senate acquitted him both times, so he was not removed from office.
